newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Prices down on low quality at Colombo tea auction.
newsitem.headline: Prices down on low quality at Colombo tea auction.

text.p: Tea prices were down at the Colombo auction on Wednesday due to limited participation by overseas buyers after the holidays and the seasonally lower quality of teas in the market, brokers said.
High growns saw fair demand at lower rates with most BOPs losing five to seven rupees and BOP fannings three to six, brokers Forbes & Walker said.
Most low growns declined by five to eight rupees with the Commonwealth of Independent States, Sri Lanka's biggest buyer, sidelined, Forbes said.

"Prices fell mainly due to the decline in quality of tea offered for sale," a Forbes broker said. "Holidays disrupt production, which in turn affect the end product. Most teas arriving in the market are not as good as other times."
The anticipated gross sale average for the 5.1 million kg on offer fell to 97 rupees from 99.26 last week, Forbes said.
"Overseas buyers too are still not working in full gear. The market is dull as a result," the broker said.
The next auction is on January 15 with 4.3 million kg on offer. --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
